ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, during the process in which a bar magnet approaches a closed metal ring from left to right, viewed from left to right, what is the direction of the induced current in the ring?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, on the left side there is a horizontally placed bar magnet, with the left end marked S and the right end marked N; above the magnet there is a velocity arrow v pointing to the right, indicating that the magnet moves from left to right. On the right side there is a vertically placed closed metal ring, the N pole of the magnet is approaching the metal ring, and the normal direction of the ring surface is along the left-right direction. Then reason: Take from left to right as the positive direction. Since the N pole of the magnet is on the left side of the ring and is approaching the ring, the direction of the original magnetic field passing through the metal ring is to the right, and as the magnet approaches, the magnetic flux to the right increases. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by the induced current should hinder this increase, so the direction of the induced magnetic field should be to the left. The question requires “viewed from left to right,” that is, the observer looks to the right from the left side, and the induced magnetic field to the left is a magnetic field pointing toward the observer. By the right-hand rule, if the magnetic field of the ring surface points toward the observer, then the direction of the current in the ring is counterclockwise.
